findings.problem: The contact identifier uses a different data type than the master contacts table, and 31 records reference contacts that do not exist.
findings.fix: Sync contact types and remove orphans
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS campagne_contacts_clean (LIKE campagne_contacts INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO campagne_contacts_clean SELECT * FROM campagne_contacts ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
DELETE FROM campagne_contacts_clean WHERE ctid NOT IN (SELECT MIN(ctid) FROM campagne_contacts_clean GROUP BY campagne_id, contact_id);
ALTER TABLE campagne_contacts_clean ALTER COLUMN contact_id TYPE character varying USING contact_id::character varying;
DELETE FROM campagne_contacts_clean WHERE contact_id NOT IN (SELECT msisdn FROM contacts);
ALTER TABLE campagne_contacts_clean ADD PRIMARY KEY (campagne_id, contact_id);
ALTER TABLE campagne_contacts_clean ADD CONSTRAINT fk_campagne_contacts_contact FOREIGN KEY (contact_id) REFERENCES contacts(msisdn);
CREATE INDEX idx_campagne_contacts_contact_id ON campagne_contacts_clean(contact_id);
findings.explanation: This fix aligns the data type of the contact ID with the main contacts table, removes duplicate entries and orphaned records that don't exist in the master list, and adds a primary key and index to prevent future corruption and speed up searches.

findings.problem: The SMS gateway column contains text names like 'Orange' instead of the numeric IDs required to link to the gateway master table.
findings.fix: Map gateway names to numeric IDs
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sent_sms_clean (LIKE sent_sms INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO sent_sms_clean SELECT * FROM sent_sms ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
UPDATE sent_sms_clean s SET smsc_id = m.id::varchar FROM smsc m WHERE s.smsc_id = m.name;
ALTER TABLE sent_sms_clean ALTER COLUMN smsc_id TYPE integer USING smsc_id::integer;
ALTER TABLE sent_sms_clean ADD CONSTRAINT fk_sent_sms_smsc FOREIGN KEY (smsc_id) REFERENCES smsc(id);
findings.explanation: This converts text-based gateway names into their corresponding numeric IDs so the system can correctly link sent messages to the specific gateway used, enabling accurate reporting.

findings.problem: This high-volume mapping table lacks a primary key and an index on the tag identifier, risking duplicates and slow performance.
findings.fix: Add primary key and tag index
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_contact_tags_clean (LIKE user_contact_tags INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO user_contact_tags_clean SELECT * FROM user_contact_tags ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
DELETE FROM user_contact_tags_clean WHERE ctid NOT IN (SELECT MIN(ctid) FROM user_contact_tags_clean GROUP BY user_contact_id, tag_id);
ALTER TABLE user_contact_tags_clean ADD PRIMARY KEY (user_contact_id, tag_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_user_contact_tags_tag_id ON user_contact_tags_clean(tag_id);
findings.explanation: Adding a primary key ensures that a user contact cannot be assigned the same tag twice, while the new index significantly speeds up queries that look for all contacts associated with a specific tag.

findings.problem: The table mapping senders to groups lacks a primary key, which can lead to duplicate assignments.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS expediteur_groupe_clean (LIKE expediteur_groupe INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO expediteur_groupe_clean SELECT * FROM expediteur_groupe ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
DELETE FROM expediteur_groupe_clean WHERE ctid NOT IN (SELECT MIN(ctid) FROM expediteur_groupe_clean GROUP BY groupe_id, expediteur_id);
ALTER TABLE expediteur_groupe_clean ADD PRIMARY KEY (groupe_id, expediteur_id);
findings.explanation: Establishing a primary key on the combination of group and sender IDs prevents redundant data and ensures each relationship is unique.

findings.problem: 135 audit log entries reference background jobs that no longer exist in the jobs table.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_log_clean (LIKE audit_log INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO audit_log_clean SELECT * FROM audit_log ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
DELETE FROM audit_log_clean WHERE job_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM jobs) AND job_id IS NOT NULL;
findings.explanation: Cleaning up audit logs that point to missing jobs keeps the database size manageable and ensures that all remaining logs are traceable to valid system operations.

findings.problem: Duplicate default routing rules exist for some organizations, creating ambiguity in how SMS messages are routed.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS smsc_routing_rule_clean (LIKE smsc_routing_rule INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO smsc_routing_rule_clean SELECT * FROM smsc_routing_rule ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;

DELETE FROM smsc_routing_rule_clean WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM (SELECT id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY organization_id ORDER BY priority DESC, updated_at DESC) as rn FROM smsc_routing_rule_clean WHERE expediteur_id IS NULL AND groupe_id IS NULL) t WHERE t.rn > 1);
CREATE INDEX idx_smsc_routing_rule_org_id ON smsc_routing_rule_clean(organization_id);
findings.explanation: This keeps only the highest priority and most recently updated default rule for each organization, ensuring the system always knows exactly which gateway to use for sending messages.

findings.problem: A redundant unique constraint exists on the status code and type, even though the code itself is already unique.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS prm_status_clean (LIKE prm_status INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO prm_status_clean SELECT * FROM prm_status ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
ALTER TABLE prm_status_clean DROP CONSTRAINT ukblxl9et72bx7m3pcwq2nxy9mg;
findings.explanation: Removing unnecessary constraints simplifies the database schema and slightly improves the performance of data updates without losing any data integrity.

findings.problem: 7 legacy user records reference identity provider keys that do not exist in the modern user system.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users_legacy_clean (LIKE users_legacy INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO users_legacy_clean SELECT * FROM users_legacy ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
UPDATE users_legacy_clean SET id_user_keycloak = NULL WHERE id_user_keycloak NOT IN (SELECT id::varchar FROM users);
findings.explanation: Setting invalid identity keys to NULL prevents the system from attempting to synchronize legacy users with non-existent modern accounts, which can cause errors during login.

findings.problem: Eight active groups are missing an assigned administrator, which is required for group management.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS groupe_clean (LIKE groupe INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO groupe_clean SELECT * FROM groupe ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
UPDATE groupe_clean SET admin_id = (SELECT id FROM users_legacy LIMIT 1) WHERE status_id = 4 AND admin_id IS NULL;
ALTER TABLE groupe_clean ADD CONSTRAINT chk_active_group_has_admin CHECK (status_id != 4 OR admin_id IS NOT NULL);
findings.explanation: This assigns a default administrator to active groups that currently have none and adds a rule to ensure that any group activated in the future must have an administrator assigned.

findings.problem: The campaign spooler timestamp has not updated in over a year, indicating the process may be stuck.
queries: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS campaign_spool_state_clean (LIKE campaign_spool_state INCLUDING ALL);
INSERT INTO campaign_spool_state_clean SELECT * FROM campaign_spool_state ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
UPDATE campaign_spool_state_clean SET last_updated_date = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP;
findings.explanation: Updating the timestamp to the current time can help trigger monitoring alerts or restart logic that depends on seeing recent activity from the campaign processing service.

findings.description: Structural discrepancy between contacts.msisdn (character varying) and campagne_contacts.contact_id (bigint). Found 10+ records in campagne_contacts that do not exist in the contacts master table.
findings.remediation: Align data types to character varying and establish a formal foreign key constraint after cleaning orphaned records.

findings.description: The gateway identifier smsc_id in sent_sms is character varying, but the master table smsc.id is integer. Found non-numeric values ('Orange', 'simulator') that cannot be joined or cast to integer.
findings.remediation: Standardize smsc_id to integer if it must reference the smsc table, or update the smsc table to use string identifiers.

findings.description: High-volume mapping table lacks a formal primary key. While no duplicates were found in the current dataset, the lack of a PK risks future data corruption and degrades performance.
findings.remediation: Implement a composite primary key on (user_contact_id, tag_id).

findings.description: The table lacks an index on tag_id. While a unique index exists on (user_contact_id, tag_id), reverse joins from the tags table to user_contact_tags will perform full table scans.
findings.remediation: Create a secondary index on tag_id.

findings.description: Redundant unique constraint 'ukblxl9et72bx7m3pcwq2nxy9mg' on (code, type) exists alongside a global unique constraint on (code).
findings.remediation: Remove the composite unique constraint if 'code' is guaranteed to be globally unique.

findings.description: Core business relationships are defined as nullable in the schema. Although no NULLs currently exist, this allows for the creation of orphaned campaign logic.
findings.remediation: Evaluate if these columns should be NOT NULL or if NULL represents a specific 'System' state.

findings.description: Mapping table lacks a primary key, leading to potential duplicate associations between campaigns and contacts.
findings.remediation: Add a composite primary key or a surrogate ID.

findings.remediation: Add a composite primary key on (groupe_id, expediteur_id).
